bib.title: Retrieval meets Long Context Large Language Models

question: Is retrieval augmentation or an extended context window better for long-context downstream tasks, and can they be combined?
hypothesis: Retrieval augmentation can match a longer context window at lower cost and still add gains on top of long-context models, at sufficient model scale.
contributions: Study of GPT-43B and Llama2-70B on 9 long-context tasks (single/multi-doc QA, query-based summarisation, few-shot ICL).
4K context plus simple retrieval is comparable to 16K context without it (29.32 vs 29.45 GPT-43B; 36.02 vs 36.78 Llama2-70B).
Retrieval still improves 16K/32K models; Llama2-70B-32k-ret (43.6) beats GPT-3.5-turbo-16k (42.8) and Davinci003.

method.summary: Extend 4K GPT-43B and Llama2 to 16K/32K by positional interpolation fine-tuned on the Pile, instruction-tune on 102K samples, then compare no-retrieval (truncated document) against top-N retrieved 300-word chunks across three retrievers on seven zero-shot datasets plus two few-shot ones.
method.task: long-context QA and query-based summarisation, zero-shot; few-shot ICL

datasets.name: Instruction blend (Soda, ELI5, FLAN, Open Assistant, Dolly, proprietary conversational)

training.objective: Context extension: positional interpolation fine-tuning (Chen et al. 2023); instruction tuning: loss on Answer tokens only
training.lr_schedule: constant (extension); not stated for instruction tuning

inference.retrieval: Documents chunked at 300 words; question and chunks encoded separately; top-N (5, 10, 20) ranked by dot product, concatenated most to least relevant; no-retrieval baseline truncates document to the sequence length; for few-shot tasks the question queries the provided examples

eval.protocol: Single run per setting; no seeds or significance tests reported. Avg-4* uses ZeroSCROLLS test scores for QM, QASP, NQA, QLTY.

results.claim: Llama2-70B 4K with top-5 retrieval (Contriever in Table 2) averages 36.02 vs 31.61 without retrieval; comparable to the 16K no-retrieval model at 36.78.
results.setup: Llama2-70B instruction-tuned, seven datasets (QM, QASP, NQA, QLTY, MSQ, HQA, MFQA), zero-shot, average score; 4K window, top-5 chunks of 300 words
results.note: Text in Sec 4.1 says 31.61 to 35.73 (Dragon, Table 4/5); Table 2 and Sec 1 use 36.02 (Contriever).

results.setup: Llama2-70B instruction-tuned, seven datasets (QM, QASP, NQA, QLTY, MSQ, HQA, MFQA), zero-shot, average score; 4K, documents truncated

results.claim: Llama2-70B 16K without retrieval averages 36.78; with top-5 retrieval 37.23; top-10 reaches 38.31 and top-20 36.61.
results.setup: Llama2-70B instruction-tuned, seven datasets (QM, QASP, NQA, QLTY, MSQ, HQA, MFQA), zero-shot, average score; 16K via positional interpolation; Dragon retriever, top-5/10/20
results.note: Top-10 (38.31) is the best 16K setting; top-20 (36.61) is below no-retrieval baseline.

results.claim: Llama2-70B 32K without retrieval averages 37.36; with top-5 retrieval (Dragon) 39.60; top-10 38.98; top-20 38.38.
results.setup: Llama2-70B instruction-tuned, seven datasets (QM, QASP, NQA, QLTY, MSQ, HQA, MFQA), zero-shot, average score; 32K via positional interpolation; Dragon retriever

results.claim: Llama2-70B 4K with Dragon retrieval: top-5 35.73, top-10 34.62, top-20 34.61 vs base 31.61.
results.setup: Llama2-70B instruction-tuned, seven datasets (QM, QASP, NQA, QLTY, MSQ, HQA, MFQA), zero-shot, average score; 4K, Dragon
results.note: Top-10 and top-20 rows at 4K have identical per-dataset scores (e.g. 42.84 MFQA), suspicious; the 4K window cannot hold 20 chunks (Table 1 avg 4,658-10,251 tokens).

results.claim: Llama2-70B-32k-ret scores 43.6 Avg-7 vs 40.9 for Llama2-70B-32k without retrieval and 42.8 for GPT-3.5-turbo-16k.
Llama2-7B 4K with top-5 retrieval averages 26.04 vs 22.65 without.
results.setup: Llama2-7B instruction tuned, seven datasets, top-5, best retriever
results.table: Table 2, rows Llama2-7B 4k and + ret 4k, column Avg.

results.claim: Llama2-7B 32K with retrieval (27.63) is slightly worse than without (28.20): retrieval does not help the small long-context model.
results.note: Text cites 'Table 5' for Llama2-7B results; they are in Table 2.
results.quote: retrieval is not helpful for both Llama2-7B-32k and ChatGLM2-6B-32k
results.table: Table 2, rows Llama2-7B 32k and + ret 32k, column Avg.

results.claim: GPT-43B 4K with top-5 retrieval averages 29.32 vs 26.44; comparable to GPT-43B 16K without retrieval at 29.45.
GPT-43B 16K with retrieval gains little: 29.65 vs 29.45.
results.table: Table 2, rows GPT-43B 16k and + ret 16k, column Avg.

results.claim: Adding more chunks does not reliably help; best averages come from top-5 or top-10, and top-20 sometimes hurts.
results.quote: adding more chunks up to 20 is not helpful and will sometime hurt the performance

results.claim: Retrieval helps few-shot tasks: Llama2-70B-ret 76 Trec and 47.3 SAMSum vs 73 and 46.5 without, GPT-3.5-turbo-16k 68 and 41.7.
results.setup: LongBench Trec and SAMSum, question used as query over few-shot examples
results.note: Text calls the model Llama2-70B-32k-ret; the table row is Llama2-70B-ret.
results.table: Table 6, row Llama2-70B-ret, columns Trec, SAMSum

results.claim: Retrieval gains hold across Dragon, Contriever and OpenAI embeddings.
A retrieval-augmented long-context model is up to 4x faster at generation than the non-retrieval one on NarrativeQA.
results.note: No timing table or hardware in the paper.
results.quote: can be much faster at generation (e.g., 4× faster on NarrativeQA)

results.claim: Llama2-70B also shows lost-in-the-middle; the 32K model uses top-5 retrieved context better than the 4K model.
results.setup: Llama2-70B-4k vs 32k, Liu et al. style position study
results.quote: we confirm that the phenomenon also exists in Llama2-70B with different context lengths

results.claim: Authors contradict LongBench: retrieval helps both short and long context models at 43B-70B scale; they attribute the difference to small (6B/7B) models.
results.setup: LongBench (Bai et al. 2023) vs this work
results.quote: we demonstrate retrieval can significantly improve the performance of both GPT-43B and Llama2-70B regardless their context window size

limits: Single runs, no seeds or variance reported.
GPT-43B is proprietary, so not reproducible.
Decoding settings, hardware, compute and optimizer not given; 4x speedup claim has no table.
Table 5 4K top-10 and top-20 rows are identical.
Open questions conceded: why more chunks hurt, lost-in-the-middle mitigation, 64k+ contexts.
GPT-3.5 is a black box, so controlled comparison is limited.
